notes.text: Saved assessment and ordered S0–S6 plan under NOTE-20260913-knowledge-backlog-implementation. Implementation is not started. Technical completion covers S0–S5 and a ready S6 procedure; actual project cutover and observation remain with the shared-project-memory parent.

problem: Current backup create opens an auto-migrating store before taking the copy; normal startup lacks future-schema rejection. Attachment publication and multi-file restore do not yet provide a durable crash-recovery protocol.
Knowledge cutover needs verified backup operations, private file handling, exclusive database ownership and recorded failure/restore evidence. The existing K7a pilot does not prove these guarantees.

risk.rollback: Keep the Git-backed source authoritative until the parent cutover gate passes. Preserve verified pre-migration and current-state copies. After new writes, reconcile those changes or repair forward instead of silently restoring an older snapshot.

scope: Follow S0–S5 in storage-safety-implementation-plan.md: agree recovery/access requirements, enforce database ownership and durable private writes, separate pre-migration backup from schema changes, harden attachment and restore durability, and deliver regular backups with recovery evidence.
Preserve the single local SQLite controller and existing application interfaces; no PostgreSQL or ORM migration is required.

Provide the S6 project-cutover procedure to the shared-project-memory parent. Real-project cutover, host account changes and operational backup destinations require their own concrete rollout scope; saving this plan does not execute them.
Keep code and repository-owned instructions in Git. Avoid two writable sources for migrated knowledge and retain a readable archival/export path.
source: Owner storage-safety discussion and request to save an implementation plan on 2026-09-28
title: Secure SQLite migrations, durable storage and recovery before knowledge cutover
validation: Backup made with the new application preserves the supported old schema before migration; backup failure prevents migration.

Supported historical fixtures migrate without data loss; future schemas are rejected before mutation; interrupted initialization and migration recover without silent reset or authentication downgrade.
Crash-point tests cover attachment publication and every restore stage, including disk-full and permission failures, corrupted or incomplete backups, unsafe paths, and foreign-key violations.
Different state directories cannot obtain independent application ownership of the same database; direct CLI creation produces private data files.
An independent restore preserves records, attachment bytes, identities, grants and history; scheduled backup failures and retention are verified against agreed recovery objectives.
Record exact-revision check/build and installed-artifact upgrade/recovery results; distinguish process interruption from unverified power-loss behavior.
value: Protect authoritative project knowledge during updates and failures, with an exercised recovery procedure and explicit limits on local-agent access.
